About

About Dr. Maryna Kuzmenko

I speak and train on AI in agriculture, for conference audiences, boards and agrifood teams, and I build the thing I talk about. MooMore uses thermal imaging and on-device AI to catch lameness in dairy cows before anyone can see it, and it won the Innovate UK Women in Innovation Award 2025/26. Before that I spent a decade on the crop side with Petiole, building measurement tools now used by research organisations on six continents. I write about all of it as a LinkedIn Top Voice, and in the AI Fluency in Agriculture book series.

What I do now

Speaking. I give keynotes, panels and guest lectures on AI in agriculture for agrifood conferences, industry meetings and universities, in person or online: topics and formats.

Training. I train agrifood teams in practical AI literacy, from a short workshop to a multi-week course — formats and topics are on team training.

Writing and coverage. I write the AI in Agriculture newsletter, host a weekly Friday LinkedIn Live on understanding agricultural AI ↗, publish explainers on YouTube ↗ and write the AI Fluency in Agriculture book series. I also report from the sector's main shows: Insights · events I've covered.

What I build

I bring nearly 10 years of practical experience in applying digital technologies in agriculture, with a primary focus on computer vision and deep learning for plant phenotyping and food quality assurance.

I am co-founder and CEO of Petiole, a UK-based SME developing practical AI tools for agriculture and plant science. The global platform Petiole Pro, developed by my team, was named a finalist in the GIST Tech-I 2015 competition in the USA, shortlisted for the UK FPC Fresh Awards 2023, and received three Innovate UK grants and one Horizon Europe grant, for practical AI applications in agricultural challenges such as pest and disease detection. Petiole Pro is used by research organisations on six continents and cited in peer-reviewed research.

I also founded MooMore ↗, an AI and thermal imaging system that detects inflammation in dairy cows before lameness develops. It won the Innovate UK Women in Innovation Award 2025/26, announced on 5 August 2026, with a £75,000 grant and a twelve-month programme running to June 2027. In validation on a 650-cow crossbred herd in Staffordshire.

The problem I keep coming back to

A measurement that matters is locked behind specialist equipment, so the people who need it never take it.

With Petiole Pro that measurement was leaf area, and the answer was a smartphone camera. With MooMore it is inflammation, and the answer is a thermal sensor. The crop and the cow are different; the shape of the problem is identical. Why I added dairy cattle to my crop AI work.
